Sonia —

Thanks for the clear ask and the deadline. We're putting together a compact appendix that maps TAM coverage, escalation tiers, and a sample incident timeline. Initial notes below; we're attaching a TAM coverage matrix and our SOC2 summary for quick review.

High-level (summary):
- TAM coverage: 24/7 global on-call for P1 incidents; regional TAMs during business hours (US/EU/APAC) for routine escalations.
- Response/SLAs: Initial response for P1/P2 within 15/60 minutes; target mitigation time dependent on incident type (detailed in matrix).
- Incident comms: Initial notification within 30 minutes of detection for P1, updates at 1h/4h/24h, and a post-incident report within 72h.
- Evidence: SOC2 summary attached, incident runbook excerpt included.

We'll provide the full appendix (TAM matrix + runbook snippets) by Feb 14 to give you time to review; final edits available before your Feb 17 internal review. If you want a 20–30 minute call to walk through the matrix, I'm available Thurs 2/12 or Mon 2/16 morning PST.

Subject: INTERNAL: proposed escalation ladder and on-call details for Tidewater appendix

Hannah / Lauren —

Draft items to include in the appendix (short bullets we can paste into the RFP spreadsheet):

1) TAM coverage model:
- Regional TAMs: US (Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 PST), EU (Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 CET), APAC (Mon–Fri 09:00–18:00 SGT). Routine support requests handled during regional business hours; SLA target: 8 business hours for non-critical issues.
- Global on-call: 24/7 severity P1/P2 handling via on-call rotation. Primary on-call phone and escalation to duty engineer.

2) Escalation ladder (who to contact and expected response):
- Tier 1 (Support): initial triage, ack within 15m for P1, 60m for P2. Contact: support@redwood.com (monitored).
- Tier 2 (TAM/SE): technical troubleshooting, contact TAM on-call, ack within 30m.
- Tier 3 (Engineering): product-level fixes, engaged by duty engineer, response within 2h for P1.
- Executive alert: SOC/CS execs notified if incident impacts >25% of production requests or SLA breach; exec call within 4h.

3) Incident comms cadence (example P1):
- 0–30m: initial notification to configured Tidewater contacts (email + PagerDuty)
- 1h: status update with current hypothesis and mitigation steps
- 4h: summary update and next steps
- 24h: interim report with timeline and RCA scope
- 72h: post-incident report + proposed remediation plan

4) Evidence/attachments we can provide: runbook extract, SOC2 summary (attached), sample incident messages and audit log exports (available on request).

Marcus — can you confirm the engineering response SLA numbers are accurate for P1?

Thanks,
Rishi
Principal Technical Program Manager
Redwood Inference
